_about: Layer 2 (product line) and layer 3 (series) of Cisco wireless, 14 Sep 2026; reviewed in layers round 3 (15 Sep 2026): no family layer — Cisco names each access-point and controller series on its own under the line ("Cisco Aironet 2800 Series", "Cisco Catalyst 9100 Access Points"), so every line of 3+ series records a no_family_reason. Access points by Cisco family and model; controllers by platform; Meraki MR bare family rows in their own line. The series ROLE is the access-point deploy_role the cup engine reads (deployRole.ts, axis ap): every role here reproduces the III.0 SKU rules row for row (checked when written: 0 changes). The Aironet 1552 is split because its models carry two roles (E/I/C outdoor, H/SA/SD/WU hazardous-location industrial). SKU prefixes AIR-, PROMO-, PPN-, KAISER- and the glued AIRAP are matched explicitly (placePart strips only 2D-/C1-/EDU-/NAL-).

re-audit decisions (operator, 15 Sep 2026, Q-12 / F-12): Cisco MobileAccessVE, the in-building cellular units sold as AIR- PIDs — the main, remote and expansion building units (AIR-330-), the access pods for CELL / PCS bands (AIR-VAP-CELLPCS) with their mounting kits (AIR-VAPMNTG-H / -V-KIT=) and the 12-port control unit (AIR-VCU-CELLPCS12). They sat in the AireOS controllers' and the Aironet access points' shared parts with kind unknown. The series carries no vendor in its name (the rows name none). Kind: the operator decided `device` for the units; `device` is not a noun of the wireless kind axis and a new noun needs its cup set, so the kind change waits for the parked kind rebuild (Q-28) and the units stay `unknown` until then

layering review of 17 Sep 2026 (fix list 2.1 / 2.2): server components and supplies of the UCS C-Series-based wireless controllers and appliances that name no platform this mapping places — CPUs, RDIMMs, MegaRAID and embedded RAID, a 32 GB SD card, a C240 M4 PCIe riser, a 650 W C-Series supply, a 500 GB drive, a UCS TPM — and the supplies named for a '9540' / '9580' controller that no series of this category names (AIR-AC-750W-R, its blanking panel, AIR-DC-950W). Cisco's end-of-sale notices list them only as 'Wireless Miscellaneous Accessories' (wireless-misc-accessories-sw-lic-eol) and 'Aironet Accessories' (aironet-accessories-eol15454), with no platform, so the series sits in the accessories line and claims no controller or appliance: the review proposed one 'Wireless controllers and appliances shared parts' series, and the rows span the AireOS controllers, the location appliances and controllers this mapping does not name. They sat in CMX 3375 / MSE 3355 / 3365 (^AIR-(MR|SD|PSU|BZL|RAID|MRAID|CPU|PCI|SVR|DC)-) and, by a label the check did not support, in Aironet Access Points shared parts (AIR-AC-750W-R, AIR-AC-750W-R-BLK, AIR-A03-D500GC3, AIR-TPM1-001). THE NAME CLAIMS NOTHING ON PURPOSE: every word of it is a labelEvidence stop word or a short word. The first name tried, 'Controller and appliance components', made 'Controller' a claim word, so the reverse check proposed 7 other controller supplies in the accessories shared parts for this series and withdrew 4 correct cross-line proposals (AIR-PSU1-770W(=) to the 5500 by '5520', AIR-PSU2V2-1200W(=) to the 8500 by '8540'); with this name both queues are the recorded 59 / 25 · ^AIR-MRAID12G, ^AIR-TPM2- (layering re-check of 17 Sep 2026, fix list section 1): AIR-MRAID12G 'Cisco 12G SAS Modular Raid Controller', AIR-MRAID12G-1GB its cache module and AIR-TPM2-001 'Trusted Platform Module 1.2 for UCS' are the same class as the MegaRAID and TPM rows here, listed by aironet-accessories-eol15454 with no platform; they sat in Wireless Antennas and Accessories shared parts by the label 'Antennas/Accessories'
